problem: Current VLN agents degrade sharply in real-world deployment. Scaling VLM backbones and training data shows diminishing returns and does not fix perceptual instability (motion blur, lighting, viewpoint shake) or under-specified instructions.
motivation: Pilot studies show that severe visual perturbations collapse SR/SPL (e.g. Qwen-based JanusVLN SPL 56.8 to 4.2 under blur). Failed episodes also have more ambiguous instructions (directional ambiguity score 51.7 vs 77.3 for successes). The authors argue that the bottleneck is not only understanding but the lack of persistent spatial goal priors and robust geometric perception.
key_idea: Render a fuzzy or precise target-location prior as a persistent visual marker on stereo egocentric views, and use stereo semantic+structure+geometry tokens with joint action and depth prediction to make a VLA navigator robust.
insight: Ablation shows the rendered target prior is the biggest single gain (SR 34.4 to 52.3 on the R2R-CE subset). Stereo 2D features add about 15 SR points (L/R 63.4 vs R/R 48.3 SR and monocular-with-prior 52.3), and depth supervision plus 3D geometry adds a further gain, with the full model reaching 72.8 SR. Structural and geometric branches need small fusion weights (0.6, 0.2) to avoid hurting semantic grounding. The prior acts as soft guidance: with 2.0 m average target noise SR is still 50.6, and OSR drops only 5.1 points. Note the headline result uses privileged goal location information that baselines do not receive.
method: Target-prior visual rendering: projects the world-frame target point into each stereo camera with pose and intrinsics, and draws a red circle; out-of-view targets are placed at the left or right image border center, updated every step.
Stereo 2D encoders: InternViT (semantic) and DINOv2 (structural) applied to left and right views, preserving binocular disparity.
3D geometry encoder: FoundationStereo-style stereo cost volume with attentive hybrid filtering, tokenized for fusion.
Unified tokens: T = αP(F_sem) + βC(F_str) + γG(V'_c), with fixed weights 1.0/0.6/0.2.

Joint action-depth prediction: the MLLM (InternVL-3.5-2B) autoregressively outputs the next 4 discrete actions, while a depth head (cost volume fusion, Soft Argmin, ConvGRU refinement, convex upsampling) predicts disparity as auxiliary supervision (λ_depth=0.1).
Two-stage training: Stage I on R2R+RxR; Stage II adds DAgger and ScaleVLN data (176 and 688 GPU hours); 8 history frames, 448x448 input.
Real-world pipeline: a GPT-based parser converts a user command into a VLN instruction plus target prior; cloud inference drives a Unitree G1 with a ZED Mini stereo camera.

setting.backbone: InternVL-3.5-2B (fine-tuned) with InternViT, DINOv2 and FoundationStereo-initialized encoders/depth head
setting.training_data: Stage I: R2R, RxR. Stage II: R2R, RxR, DAgger, ScaleVLN. The 'no external data' variant uses standard navigation data only.
setting.observation: stereo egocentric RGB (left/right) with 8 history frames plus a rendered target-point marker
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: forward 0.25 m, turn left/right 15°, stop (predicts 4 future actions)
setting.privileged: Target-location prior (GT goal point, or noisy version) rendered as input, in simulation and real world (from the instruction parser); no depth sensor. The simulator uses stereo cameras with a 0.1 m baseline.

numbers_note: The ablation (Table 2b) is on an unspecified subset of R2R-CE, so it is not included. Real-world results are per-scenario success rates (macro average 60.6%), with no benchmark numbers.
results: StereoNav (2B-based, listed as 3B) reaches 81.1 SR / 68.3 SPL on R2R-CE val-unseen and 67.5 SR / 52.0 SPL on RxR-CE, the best among egocentric RGB agents (previous best R2R-CE SR was 64.7, SACA/AgentVLN 67.2 for RGB-D). Without extra data it still gets 72.8 SR. In real-world tests on a Unitree G1 it averages 60.6% success versus 24.3% for StreamVLN and 22.1% for DreamNav, and it degrades far less under motion blur and viewpoint oscillation.
limitations: Requires an explicit or implicit target-location prior as input and cannot work without one; the comparison against baselines that do not get goal-location information is not equal.
Performance drops sharply as the prior gets noisy (3.0 m preset deviation: SR 50.6, SPL 33.0), and SPL is more sensitive than OSR.
Real-world evaluation is small (about 45 trials per scenario, no variance), and RxR-CE SPL/NE trail panoramic and RGB-D agents.
